items.title: Polish lektor wins first AI voice deepfake ruling
items.excerpt: A Warsaw court ruled on 13 November that adverts using an AI copy of film reader Jarosław Łukomski's voice were a deepfake, ordering removal, apologies and damages. In Poland's first cloned-voice trial, the judge said the protection covers anyone's voice, not only famous ones — a precedent for narrators and audiobook voices.

items.title: Kakao, OpenAI Collaborate on AI-Generated Short Animation Based on Ryan Begins Webtoon
items.excerpt: Kakao and OpenAI released an AI-generated short animation adapted from the Ryan Begins webtoon; the production team said it used roughly 1,500 prompts for a single scene to reach the intended direction and emotional tone.

items.title: The Anatomy of "Harm": An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO discusses the federation's study detailing the harm generative AI causes to publishers and authors, and what it means for collective licensing and copyright policy.

items.title: From AI Adoption to AI Practice: Building Governed AI in Scholarly Publishing
items.excerpt: How a publisher can make AI useful across the organization while keeping control of confidential information, editorial decisions and accountability — a practical governance framework for in-house AI.

items.title: Ask the Technology Providers: Our Charleston Conversation
items.excerpt: Takeaways from a Charleston Conference panel on AI's impact on libraries, publishers and platforms, including US vs EU approaches to AI watermarking and traceability.

items.title: In France, the Publishing Industry Endures an Autumn of Discontent
items.excerpt: The use of AI in writing novels — after the Goncourt winner's admission — is roiling a French book business already under pressure, alongside debates over patriarchy and right-wing media influence.

items.title: Around the Book World: Monday, November 9, 2026 (Robert Laffont vs Gallimard on AI manuscript screening)
items.excerpt: Robert Laffont's managing director Frédéric Martin opposes using AI-detection software to screen submissions, saying author-publisher relations should rest on trust — while Gallimard parent Madrigall plans to screen manuscripts for AI.

items.title: [이연숙의 독락(讀樂) 교실] AI는 왜 훔쳐서까지 소설을 읽었을까
items.excerpt: 한강의 『소년이 온다』 등이 앤트로픽에 의해 무단 내려받기된 논란을 계기로, AI 학습과 문학 저작권이 독자와 작가에게 던지는 질문을 짚는 칼럼.

items.title: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world
items.excerpt: With authors losing lucrative deals and writers removed from prize shortlists, accusations of AI use are sending shock waves through publishing; the Guardian asks whether it is too late to turn the tide on machine writing.

items.title: New French literary prize will reward work created with AI help
items.excerpt: The new Prix Pascal, chaired by Jacques Attali, will honor an unpublished French text written with Claude, Gemini or ChatGPT; entrants must declare the LLM or agents used and submit a technical file plus a two-page note on the project's 'seed', with submissions open until end of November.

items.title: Op-Ed: Should We Care If African Writers Are Using AI?
items.excerpt: After the Caine Prize AI allegations, this op-ed argues the discourse ignores a fundamental question and reveals an African literary scene yet to renegotiate old assumptions about literary authenticity.

items.title: 대만서도 'AI 대량 책 매입' 논란…"문화부, 출판산업 영향 파악해야"
items.excerpt: 앤트로픽이 대만 도서유통사 연합발행(UDC)에서 2024년 11월부터 올해 9월까지 563톤의 책을 사들인 사실이 알려지며 대만 입법원에서 문화부 장관에게 출판산업 영향 파악을 요구하는 등 논란이 정치권으로 번지고 있다.

items.title: [만나보니] '퇴마록' 이우혁 "AI는 고통 이해 못해…창작 도구에 불과"
items.excerpt: 『퇴마록』 작가 이우혁이 AI 시대 창작에 대해 'AI는 인간의 고통을 아는 척할 뿐 느끼지 못한다'며 AI는 창작 도구에 불과하다고 말했다.

items.title: When AI writes, what remains human?
items.excerpt: From literary prizes to Korean campuses, AI-assisted writing is forcing a reckoning over authorship and trust.

items.title: Sharjah Book Fair Lets Visitors Call Literary Icons Through AI
items.excerpt: Visitors to the 45th Sharjah International Book Fair can 'phone' AI recreations of literary icons, an installation that turns generative voice and conversation tech into a reader-engagement exhibit.

items.title: AI Translation is a Long Way Off for Visual Novels
items.excerpt: MAGES president Makoto Asada says AI translation isn't yet good enough for visual novels because human review and nuanced language work are still needed; the writer argues AI fails on dialects, idioms and wordplay.

items.title: Copyright agreements allow use of content for AI prompts
items.excerpt: New Zealand's Tāwhia Copyright Aotearoa (formerly Copyright Licensing New Zealand) has signed a bilateral agreement with the UK's Copyright Licensing Agency that lets licensed content be used in AI prompts.

items.title: SHERRY PRESTON: AI-generated books prompt closer scrutiny at libraries
items.excerpt: A librarian explains why she now scrutinizes nonfiction titles before adding them to the shelves, as AI-generated books slip into library acquisition channels.

items.title: 'AI slop' installed in upgraded Brisbane library faces criticism
items.excerpt: Brisbane City Council was criticised for using AI to create a mural in the children's section of the renovated Bulimba Library; children's book illustrator Sophie Beer labelled it 'AI slop'.
